title: GeM Strengthens Participation of MSMEs, Startups, Women Entrepreneurs and SHGs
subtitle: MSME Procurement through GeM Reaches ₹2.37 Lakh Crore in FY 2025–26
body_text:
The number of MSMEs, start-ups, women entrepreneurs and Self-Help Groups (SHGs) registered on the Government e-Marketplace (GeM), category-wise, as on 30th July, 2026, is as below:
Seller Group All India Karnataka Bengaluru MSMEs 11,75,001 55,053 16,091 Startups 37,758 2,772 1,951 Women Entrepreneurs 2,17,155 10,896 3,052 SHGs 3,784 266 09
Yes, procurement from MSMEs through GeM has increased during the last five years. The details of procurement from MSMEs through GeM during the last five financial years are as under:
FY Total Order Value (₹ in Cr) MSME Order Value (₹ in Cr) Proportion of Procurement FY21-22 1,06,597 59,033 0.554 FY22-23 2,01,317 97,332 0.483 FY23-24 4,03,569 1,90,485 0.472 FY24-25 5,41,602 1,95,976 0.362 FY25-26 5,02,776 2,37,235 0.472
GeM has started utilising AI/ML based analytical models to identify suspicious procurement patterns, including potential buyer-seller collusion, abnormal pricing and repeated participation patterns. These models help in identifying cases pertaining to Order Splitting, suspected Buyer Seller Collusion based on the similar digital footprints, Bidder's qualification ratio, procurement prices vis-a-vis product median prices etc. The cases flagged through these analytical tools are made accessible to the concerned authorities within the buyer organizations for further review and necessary action.
GeM tries to leverage upon the Competition Commission of India (CCI) toolkit to identify any suspected cartels, based on the bidder's digital footprints, like IP address, bid pricing, submission timings etc. GeM has established an Incident Management framework under which violations relating to submission of false documents, fraudulent practices, collusive behaviour and other misconduct are examined and appropriate administrative action, including suspension, and other measures as per GeM policies, are regularly taken.
The number of sellers suspended during the last three financial years and are as under:
FY Incident Raised Seller Suspended 2023-24 1,96,793 72,902 2024-25 1,96,803 62,091 2025-26 1,81,035 55,772
The main reasons for suspension include:
Listing the products/services in wrong category or with wrong specifications. Unreasonable offer price Delay in Delivery as per contract Refuses to supply products/services after placement of contract.
GeM has implemented multiple safeguards to strengthen vendor verification and procurement integrity, including the following:
GeM has a fully online vendor registration process. GeM has deployed advanced analytics tools to detect procurement anomalies such as order splitting, suspicious bidding, abnormal pricing and potential collusion, with flagged cases reflected on primary buyer's dashboards for action.
Anti-competitive behaviour or cartel formation is classified as a Severe/Grave deviation under GeM's Incident Management framework, with proven cases attracting suspension of up to 365 days.
This information was given by Minister of State for Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Shri Jitin Prasada in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.
***
Abhishek Dayal/Shabbir Azad/Anushka Pandey

enrichment.summary: In a written Rajya Sabha reply on 11 August 2026, MoS Commerce & Industry Jitin Prasada gave data on GeM's registered MSMEs, startups, women entrepreneurs and SHGs as of 30 July 2026, and noted MSME procurement through GeM rose to ₹2.37 lakh crore in FY 2025-26. He also detailed GeM's use of AI/ML analytics and CCI's cartel-detection toolkit to flag suspicious procurement patterns, and disclosed seller suspension figures for the last three fiscal years due to incidents like wrong listings, unreasonable pricing and delivery delays.
enrichment.context:
The Government e-Marketplace (GeM), launched in 2016, is the online platform through which central and state government departments, PSUs and other public entities procure goods and services, with a mandated preference for procurement from Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) as per the Public Procurement Policy for MSEs, which mandates a minimum 25% procurement from MSEs by central ministries/CPSEs, including sub-targets for women-owned and SC/ST-owned enterprises. GeM has been positioned as a transparency and efficiency tool that reduces human interface in government procurement while widening market access for small vendors, startups and self-help groups (SHGs), aligning with the Atmanirbhar Bharat and Make in India objectives.

The data shows that while total order value through GeM has grown substantially over five years (from about ₹1.07 lakh crore in FY21-22 to over ₹5 lakh crore in FY25-26), the *proportion* of procurement going to MSMEs has actually declined from 55.4% in FY21-22 to under 50% in recent years, even though absolute MSME procurement value has grown. This raises questions about whether large-scale procurement growth is disproportionately benefiting larger vendors. The government's increasing reliance on AI/ML-based anomaly detection and collaboration with the Competition Commission of India (CCI) reflects a broader push toward using technology for fraud prevention, cartel detection and probity in public procurement, an area of growing policy focus given the scale of government spending routed through digital platforms.

prelims_questions.question: The Government e-Marketplace (GeM) is primarily used for which of the following purposes?
options: Facilitating online procurement of goods and services by government departments and public sector entities
Providing subsidised credit to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
Registering land records digitally across states
Disbursing direct benefit transfers to farmers
prelims_questions.explanation: GeM is the online platform through which central/state government departments, PSUs and other public entities procure goods and services from registered sellers, including MSMEs, startups, women entrepreneurs and SHGs.

prelims_questions.question: Which body's toolkit does GeM utilise to help identify suspected cartel formation based on bidders' digital footprints such as IP addresses and bid submission timings?
options: Securities and Exchange Board of India
prelims_questions.explanation: As stated in the release, GeM leverages the Competition Commission of India's (CCI) toolkit to detect suspected cartels based on bidders' digital footprints.
